angle: It works a single biased-coin distribution all the way from the mean through the squared variable to the variance computed both directly and via the shortcut, closing with a million-draw simulation of convergence.
angle_detail: Study [04:27]-[06:01] first for the mean 1 point 2 calculation as a probability-weighted average, then [08:16]-[11:12] for the variance 0 point 48 with the shortcut verification and the square root for the standard deviation. Use the simulation at [06:35]-[07:32] to cement why long-run averages settle near the theoretical mean, and remember the early warning that expectation is a mean rather than the most likely or even a possible value. The video stays discrete only, so look elsewhere for densities, transformations, or covariance.
